description: How a game engine works inside and how to build one: the game loop and timing, rendering sprites and scenes, input handling, entity and component systems, collision detection, audio, resource management and performance on low-end phones. Students write a small engine in JavaScript on the HTML canvas and WebGL piece by piece, profile it in the browser and ship a complete game on it.
modelledOn: McShaffry and Graham, Game Coding Complete
outcomes: Explain the architecture of a game engine and the responsibilities of its runtime subsystems.
Implement a game loop with fixed and variable time steps, frame pacing and interpolation.
Render sprites, tile maps and scenes efficiently with the canvas and WebGL, using batching, atlases and cameras.
Design entity and component systems and apply game programming patterns to organise game code.
Implement collision detection with bounding volumes and spatial partitioning, and integrate input and audio subsystems.
Profile and optimise a game to run smoothly on low-end Android phones with limited memory, CPU and battery.

units.title: Engine architecture and the game loop
topics: What an engine is: runtime layers (platform, core systems, resources, rendering, physics, gameplay) and the tools pipeline
The game loop: process input, update, render; requestAnimationFrame and the browser event loop
Time: delta time, fixed time step with accumulator, interpolation between states, spiral of death
Frame rate, vertical sync, frame pacing and measuring frame time
Engine start-up and shut-down, configuration, logging and a debug overlay

units.title: Rendering sprites and scenes
topics: 2D rendering with the canvas: sprites, transforms, layering and draw order
Sprite sheets and texture atlases; frame-based and skeletal animation; animation state machines
Tile maps: tile sets, layers, culling to the visible area, map editors and loading map files
Cameras and viewports: following, dead zones, screen shake, parallax and resolution independence
WebGL sprite batching: vertex buffers, a textured-quad shader, minimising draw calls and state changes
Scene graphs, render queues and particle effects

units.title: Input handling
topics: Input devices in the browser: keyboard, mouse, touch, pointer events and gamepads
Polling versus events; input buffering and mapping raw input to game actions
Touch controls for phones: virtual joysticks, gestures, tap zones and hit-target sizing
Input latency, debouncing and combos; recording and replaying input for testing

units.title: Entity and component systems
topics: From inheritance hierarchies to composition: the problems with deep game-object class trees
Entity-component-system architecture: entities as identifiers, components as data, systems as behaviour
Data-oriented design: structure of arrays, cache locality, archetypes and sparse sets
Game programming patterns: command, observer, state, component, object pool, update method, service locator
Messaging and events between systems; scripting gameplay and hot reloading
Saving and loading game state; serialisation of entities and components

units.title: Collision detection
topics: Bounding volumes: circles, axis-aligned bounding boxes, oriented boxes and capsules; intersection tests
The separating axis theorem for convex polygons; point-in-polygon and ray casts
Broad phase: uniform grids, quadtrees, sweep and prune, bounding volume hierarchies
Continuous collision detection and tunnelling; swept tests
Collision layers and masks, triggers and resolving overlaps for tile-based and platform games
Measuring broad-phase performance as the number of entities grows

units.title: Audio
topics: Digital audio basics: sampling, formats, compression and latency
The Web Audio API: audio context, buffers, gain and panning nodes, the browser autoplay policy
A sound manager: channels, priorities, pooling, music crossfades and ducking
Positional audio, procedural sound effects and keeping audio in sync with gameplay

units.title: Resources, scenes and tools
topics: Resource management: loading, caching, reference counting and unloading assets
Asset pipelines: image compression, atlasing, audio encoding and bundling for the web
Scene management, transitions and loading screens; progressive loading on slow connections
Debugging tools: in-game console, entity inspector, collision visualisation and time scaling
Offline play with service workers and caching for intermittent connectivity

units.title: Performance on low-end phones
topics: The target: entry-level Android phones with little RAM, slow CPUs and GPUs, and expensive mobile data
Profiling in the browser: frame timelines, CPU profiles, memory snapshots and GPU bottlenecks
Avoiding garbage-collection pauses: object pools, preallocated arrays and avoiding per-frame allocations
Reducing draw calls, overdraw and fill-rate cost; lower resolutions and adaptive quality settings
Battery, thermal throttling, download size and start-up time as design constraints

units.title: Capstone: a complete game on the engine
topics: Integrating the subsystems: loop, renderer, input, ECS, collision and audio into one engine
Building a complete 2D game, such as a platformer about an Ananse story or an arcade game set in a Ghanaian market
Testing on a real low-end phone and meeting a frame-time and memory budget
Packaging as a progressive web app and documenting the engine's architecture

schedule.title: Engine layers and the game loop
schedule.exercise: Draw the layer diagram of a small 2D engine and write one sentence on what each layer may and may not depend on.

tasks.title: Write a game loop with requestAnimationFrame that moves a square across a canvas and shows its frame count on screen
Implement a fixed time step with an accumulator and run it at 30 and 144 Hz displays to show the physics gives identical results
Reproduce the spiral of death by making update slower than the step, then add a frame clamp and interpolation to fix it

schedule.title: Frame pacing and engine start-up
schedule.exercise: Write a half-page note on why average frame rate hides stutter and which two measurements you would report instead.

tasks.title: Measure frame time for 300 frames and print the average, the worst frame and the percentage of frames over 16.7 ms
Build a debug overlay showing FPS, frame time graph and entity count, toggled by a key, and log engine start-up and shut-down steps
Compare the frame pacing of a loop with and without vsync-aware timing under a simulated load, and chart the jitter for each

schedule.title: 2D rendering, sprites and tile maps
schedule.exercise: Sketch the layer order of a market scene with ground, stalls, characters and signs, and justify the draw order and any sorting rule.

tasks.title: Draw layered sprites on a canvas with translation, rotation and scaling, and sort them so characters pass behind and in front of stalls
Animate a character from a sprite sheet with an animation state machine for idle, walk and jump, driven by keyboard input
Load a tile map from a JSON file with three layers, draw only the visible tiles, and measure the draw count against drawing the full map

schedule.title: Cameras, WebGL batching and effects
schedule.exercise: Explain in writing how reducing draw calls speeds up a renderer, using the numbers from your batching test.

tasks.title: Add a camera that follows the player with a dead zone and screen shake, and keep the pixel scale correct at two window sizes
Write a WebGL textured-quad shader and draw 1000 sprites in one batched call, then compare frame time with 1000 separate draw calls
Build a scene graph with parent-child transforms, a render queue sorted by layer, and a particle emitter, then profile 5000 particles

schedule.title: Input handling
schedule.exercise: Design a control scheme for a platformer on both keyboard and touch, listing each action, its input and its on-screen target size.

tasks.title: Read keyboard, mouse and touch events and display the current state of each input on screen with a live readout
Map raw inputs to named actions with rebinding, and add an input buffer so a jump pressed 100 ms early still registers
Record a play session as timestamped inputs, replay it deterministically on a fixed step, and verify that both runs end in the same state

schedule.title: Game object architecture
schedule.exercise: Write a short argument for or against deep inheritance trees for game objects, using one example of a flying, shooting, burning enemy.

tasks.title: Refactor a three-level inheritance hierarchy of enemies into composed components and show a new enemy type built without a new class
Build a minimal entity-component-system with entity ids, component stores and a movement system, and run it on 1000 entities
Compare an array-of-objects layout with a structure-of-arrays layout for 100000 entities and measure the update time of each

schedule.title: Patterns, messaging and saving
schedule.exercise: Pick three patterns from the course, and for each explain the problem it solves in your game and the cost it adds.

tasks.title: Implement an object pool for bullets and an observer for score events, and show that pooled bullets never allocate during play
Add an event bus between collision, audio and scoring systems so none depends directly on another, and demonstrate hot reloading of a script
Serialise all entities and components to JSON, reload the saved state, and check that a replay from the save matches the original run

schedule.title: Collision detection geometry
schedule.exercise: Prove by hand that two circles overlap exactly when the distance between centres is less than the sum of radii, then extend the idea to boxes.

tasks.title: Implement circle and axis-aligned box intersection tests and display overlapping shapes in a different colour
Implement the separating axis test for convex polygons and a ray cast, and visualise the axis that separates two non-colliding shapes
Add a quadtree broad phase to 2000 moving circles and measure how many pair tests it avoids compared with testing every pair

schedule.title: Fast objects and collision performance
schedule.exercise: Write a short report on how collision layers keep a platformer simple, listing the layers and masks for player, enemies, coins and walls.

tasks.title: Set up collision layers and masks so coins collide only with the player, and a trigger zone that logs when the player enters
Fire a fast bullet through a thin wall to show tunnelling, then fix it with a swept test and verify that all hits register
Plot broad-phase time against entity count for grid, quadtree and sweep and prune, and choose the best method for 500 and for 5000 entities

schedule.title: Audio
schedule.exercise: Describe the audio design for a market arcade game: the sound list, which sounds can overlap, and which one may interrupt another.

tasks.title: Load and play a sound with the Web Audio API after a user gesture, with gain and stereo pan controls driven by sliders
Write a sound manager with channels, priorities and pooling that limits simultaneous sounds and crossfades between two music tracks
Generate sound effects procedurally with oscillators and envelopes, position them in stereo by on-screen location, and keep them in step with gameplay

schedule.title: Resources, assets and debugging tools
schedule.exercise: Write a plan for loading assets on a slow mobile connection, stating which assets load first, which are lazy and what the player sees meanwhile.

tasks.title: Write a resource manager that loads an image once, caches it, counts references and unloads it when no scene uses it
Build scene transitions with a loading screen that shows real progress while three asset bundles load in sequence
Add a service worker that caches the game for offline play, then test an update that replaces the cache without breaking a running session

schedule.title: Performance on low-end phones
schedule.exercise: Create a performance budget table for an entry-level Android phone covering frame time, memory, download size and start-up time.

tasks.title: Record a browser performance profile of your game for ten seconds and identify the three functions that use the most time
Remove per-frame allocations from a particle system using preallocated arrays, then show the garbage-collection pauses disappear in the profile
Implement adaptive quality that lowers resolution and particle count when frame time exceeds budget, and test it under a simulated slow CPU

schedule.title: Integration and capstone
schedule.exercise: Capstone report: document the architecture, the frame-time and memory results on a low-end device, and the three biggest lessons from building the game.

tasks.title: Connect the loop, renderer, input and collision modules into one engine skeleton that runs a moving player with a camera and a solid wall
Build a complete level of an Ananse story platformer with enemies, collectibles, sound and a win condition running at 60 frames per second
Meet a budget of 16 ms per frame and 100 MB of memory on a throttled device, documenting each optimisation and its measured effect
